key_insight: Multi-agent collaboration is not always beneficial: as language models become more capable, they can outperform collaborative setups in some tasks and settings. The paper also shows that a predictive model can choose the best architecture with 87% accuracy on held-out within-domain configurations.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the question of when multi-agent LLM collaboration helps, when it hurts, and how to automatically choose the best single-agent or multi-agent architecture for a given task.
method: Ran a controlled study across 260 multi-agent and single-agent configurations.
Compared performance across different model capacities, collaboration patterns, and architecture choices.
Trained a predictive selector to estimate which architecture will work best for a given setting.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this means collaboration should be treated as a design choice rather than a default improvement. The results can save compute and reduce complexity by helping teams deploy the simplest architecture that performs best.
visual_elements: A decision flowchart showing when to use single-agent vs multi-agent setups
A performance comparison bar chart across 260 configurations
A heatmap of task performance versus model capability and collaboration level
An architecture selection diagram highlighting the predictive model choosing the best setup
paper_title: Capable language models can outgrow the benefits of collaboration
paper_authors: Yubin Kim, Ken Gu, Chanwoo Park, Chunjong Park, Samuel Schmidgall
